biggest_catch: You must be an active residential Consumers Energy electric or combination customer, and the appliance must be in working order — a dead fridge they haul away earns you nothing. Small appliances ($15) only qualify when picked up alongside a qualifying large appliance.
catches: Appliances must be working (cooling) at pickup — non-working units don't qualify.
Two large appliances and four small appliances maximum per year.
Small appliance rebates ($15) are only available with a qualifying large appliance pickup.
You must have an active residential Consumers Energy electric or combination account at the service address.
Free pickup is scheduled by the program — you can't just drop units off.

c2.evidence: Official program page states: $50 rebate per full-size refrigerator or freezer, $15 for qualifying small appliances, with free pickup.

c3.evidence: Free pickup; no enrollment or participation fee.

c4.evidence: Official page states the rebate is paid after the scheduled pickup of the qualifying appliance.

steps: Check that you have an active residential Consumers Energy electric or combination account.
Make sure your old full-size refrigerator or freezer still works (it must cool at pickup).
Schedule your free pickup through the appliance-recycling program page or by phone.
Have the working appliance plugged in and accessible on pickup day.
Receive the $50 rebate after pickup ($15 each for qualifying small appliances picked up with it).
